claims: C1 the example contrasts a good response that gives an overview and asks which detail to focus on with a bad response that overloads the user with detail
C2 the good response is preferred for an open-ended planning question
C3 the bad response is dispreferred because it dumps the full detail list at once

concepts.name: voice_turn_taking_rule
concepts.gloss: a rule that voice responses must align with iterative, turn-taking conversation structure and adapt to conversational shifts

concepts.name: overview_then_detail_response
concepts.gloss: a response that gives a brief overview of the topic and asks the user which aspect to focus on, rather than listing all details at once

concepts.name: overloads_with_detail
concepts.gloss: a response that presents the full detailed list of considerations at once, overwhelming the user

concepts.name: open_planning_question
concepts.gloss: a user question that asks broadly what to consider while planning an event, admitting many possible answers

concepts.name: answers_question
concepts.gloss: response R answers user question Q
concepts.inference: the example relates each assistant response to the user's planning question it answers

ontology.gloss: R is a response that gives an overview and asks which detail to focus on
R is a response that overloads the user with detail

asserts.read_back: responding with % is preferred: an overview with an offer to focus on a specific aspect suits an open-ended planning question
responding with % is dispreferred: it overloads the user with detail instead of offering an overview first

closure.reason: the example states a preference between two permitted responses; it forbids nothing, so silence leaves responses permitted
